patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff moves `memset(residual, 0, residual_len)` ahead of the parse and removes the old empty-suffix-only clear. The patched-source fixed rebuild in the reused vulnerable workspace failed during the fallback full build for environment reasons, so fixed-side execution used the authoritative `n132/arvo:32482-fix` image. That fixed original still executes the same non-empty residual path and records the residual buffer as fully initialized before and after the partial copy.
verification_limitations: Fixed-side execution used the authoritative `-fix` image after the patched-source full rebuild in the reused workspace failed with `configure: error: cannot run C compiled programs`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled config text into the parser callback string. `lxc_iterate_parts` expands to `strtok_r`, so with this witness the first `line` available to `parse_line()` ends at the embedded NUL as `lxc.time.offset.bootpt=\t1.\t`.

The helper clears `residual` only on the empty-suffix path. When `strtoll()` leaves any non-empty residual string, this block is skipped and the later short copy writes into caller storage that may still contain uninitialized bytes.

MSan crash site in the staged reproducing checkout. The first `strlen(buffer)` treats the caller's partially initialized `buf` as a C string and scans into poisoned stack byte `buf[1]` while searching for a terminator.

On the non-empty suffix path, `memcpy(residual, remaining, len)` writes only the parsed `.` suffix into the residual buffer and, on the vulnerable execution, leaves the remaining two bytes uninitialized.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `residual_partial_copy.residual_initialized_prefix_len=1` and `residual_partial_copy.residual_len=3` immediately after `memcpy(residual, remaining, len)`.

edges.description: The same `residual` buffer whose missing initialization is observed at the root site is the destination buffer consumed by the later partial `memcpy` on the non-empty suffix path.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `residual_root_state.residual_ptr == residual_partial_copy.residual_ptr`.

edges.description: The partially initialized residual buffer produced by the short `memcpy` is passed unchanged into `lxc_trim_whitespace_in_place()` and becomes the `buffer` argument consumed by the crashing `strlen` sink.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `residual_partial_copy.residual_ptr == trim_strlen_sink.buffer_ptr`.
